Roofing in Lancaster, Texas

Lancaster has rebuilt after two tornadoes in 18 years, and today it asks every roofer to register with the city before taking a permit. One free call puts you through to an independent roofing company that works in Lancaster.

Call (469) 649-7066 Lancaster's roofer rules
  1. Home
  2. Service Areas
  3. Lancaster

A town that has rebuilt its roofs before

Ask anyone who has lived in Lancaster for thirty years about roofing and the conversation tends to start with April 25, 1994. At 9:38 that night, one or more tornadoes went through the heart of town. A state historical marker on the square records three deaths and more than 200 homes and 26 businesses destroyed or badly damaged. The junior high, the library and City Hall all needed major repair.

The square had already burned once and come back in brick after fires in 1877 and 1889; in 1994 the storm hit it hard again. Eighteen years later, on April 3, 2012, another tornado cut across the north side of Lancaster on its way into south Dallas.

Lancaster sits in southern Dallas County, about fifteen minutes south of downtown Dallas, and counted 41,275 residents in 2020. Roofing in Lancaster, TX today runs under city rules that are stricter than many people expect, and they are the place to start.

Lancaster wants roofers on its books before the job

Texas has no state license for roofing, so the state never checks who is on your roof. The City of Lancaster fills part of that gap with its own registration. Its development handbook says builders and subcontractors must be registered with the city, and the contractor registration form names roofing contractors among the trades it covers.

Registration, renewed yearly

A registration is good for one year from the day it is issued. The 2025 to 2026 fee schedule lists building and general contractor registration at $100 a year. If someone other than the company owner registers, or it is done by mail, the form must be notarized.

Liability coverage on record

The form asks for a general liability policy of at least $500,000, with the City of Lancaster listed as certificate holder. That is coverage the city sees; ask the roofer's insurer to send you a certificate too.

A $100 roofing permit

The same fee schedule lists a roofing permit at $100. Registered contractors apply, track the permit and request inspections through the city's online portal.

The permit on the fence

Lancaster's handbook says a copy of the permit must be posted at the job site the whole time work goes on. If tear-off starts and nothing is posted, ask why before the next bundle goes up.

Questions about whether a company is registered go to the Building Division at (972) 218-1200, at City Hall, 211 N. Henry Street. The permit technicians answer at (972) 218-1201 and (972) 218-1205. Fees and forms change, so confirm the current rules before work starts.

Two Lancaster tornadoes, side by side

The two storms were very different, and both did heavy damage to homes in town.

DetailApril 25, 1994April 3, 2012
Where it hitThe center of town at 9:38 p.m., including the historic squareDamage from east of I-35E and Parkerville Road northeast across I-20 into south Dallas
Strength recordedF4 on the old Fujita scale, as listed in the record of the April 1994 outbreak; the marker says one or more tornadoesEF-2 per the National Weather Service in Fort Worth, winds near 130 mph
SizeAbout six miles long and up to half a mile wide, per accounts of the outbreak200 yards wide; the weather service survey of the Lancaster and Dallas damage ran about 7.1 miles
Damage noted3 deaths; over 200 homes and 26 businesses destroyed or badly damaged, per the historical markerHeaviest near Wintergreen Road, Telephone Road and North Dallas Road; a trucking facility hit at I-20

The 2012 storm lifted near Bonnie View Road and Memory Lane in Dallas. When Lancaster's mayor spoke to reporters that week, he said the last bad tornado had been in 1994. Between storms of that size, it is ordinary spring hail and straight-line wind that wear Lancaster roofs down.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Before you sign with a Lancaster roofer

Because the city keeps a list, you can check more here than in many towns. Use it, and then ask the questions the city does not.

  1. Registration. Is your registration with Lancaster current for this year, and under what company name?
  2. Permit. When will you file the roofing permit through the portal, and where will the posted copy hang?
  3. Inspection. Who requests the city inspection, and will you send me the result?
  4. Insurance. Will your insurer email me a certificate, the same coverage you filed with the city?
  5. Scope. Does the written quote list tear-off, decking by the sheet, underlayment, flashing, vents and cleanup?
  6. Warranty. How long is your labor warranty, what does the paper say it covers, and who registers the shingle warranty?

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

What the line does for Lancaster callers

DFW Expert Roofers is a phone line, not a roofer. It does not register with the city, pull permits or set foot on a roof. It answers, asks a few questions and connects you.

  1. Dial the lineAn automated assistant picks up (469) 649-7066 any time and asks what you need. The same number also takes air conditioning, heating and pressure washing calls, so say "roof".
  2. Tell it about the roofHail, a drip in the ceiling, shingles in the yard, a tree limb, or an aging roof you want checked, plus your town and how soon you need someone.
  3. Get transferredThe call goes to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works in Dallas-Fort Worth. It hears a quick summary of your call before it answers.
  4. Work with that companyIt inspects, prices and does the job, and you pay it (or your insurer does, as you arrange). If it cannot pick up, it gets your name, number, town and need so it can call you back.

Hail on the lawn, a stain over the hallway, or an older roof you want looked at before the next spring? Call and say what you see. The Lancaster-area roofer you reach checks the roof in person and writes up its price.

What Lancaster homeowners ask about roofing

Does a roofer need to be registered in Lancaster TX?

Yes. Lancaster's development handbook says builders and subcontractors must be registered with the city, and its contractor registration form lists roofing contractors as one of the types. Registration lasts one year, the fee schedule sets building and general contractor registration at $100 a year, and the form asks for at least $500,000 in general liability coverage with the city named on the certificate. Ask the Building Division at (972) 218-1200 to confirm a company is on file.

How much is a roofing permit in Lancaster?

The city's 2025 to 2026 master fee schedule lists a roofing permit at $100. Only a registered contractor can apply through Lancaster's online permit portal, so on a hired job the roofer files it and the fee usually shows up in the quote. Ask whether it is included. A copy of the permit has to stay posted at the job site, which gives you an easy way to see it with your own eyes.

Was Lancaster hit by a tornado in 2012?

Yes. On April 3, 2012, a tornado moved northeast across Lancaster into south Dallas. The National Weather Service office in Fort Worth rated it EF-2, with winds near 130 mph and a width of 200 yards. Its survey traced damage for about 7.1 miles, starting east of Interstate 35E and Parkerville Road. The worst damage was near Wintergreen Road, Telephone Road and North Dallas Road.

Who do I call for roofing in Lancaster TX after a storm?

Call DFW Expert Roofers and say "roof" when the assistant asks. It takes your street, what you see and how urgent it is, then transfers you to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Lancaster calls. That company inspects and quotes; the line does neither. Until a roofer arrives, stay off the roof and follow the steps after storm damage.

A Lancaster roof question? Call free

Say what the roof is doing and which town you are in. The automated assistant passes you to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works in DFW. That company comes out, looks at the roof and prices the job itself.
